summary: A surface that holds one thing, and says so with a border and a little lift.

pairs.dont: Put three unrelated sections in one card because they share a screen.
pairs.do: Give each its own card, or drop the card and use headings.
pairs.why: The border is a claim that everything inside belongs together. Used on a grab bag it stops meaning anything, and the page reads as boxes rather than content.

pairs.dont: Nest a card inside a card.
pairs.do: Use a divider, a heading, or a plain bordered region inside.
pairs.why: Two borders and two shadows say "unit" twice about the same content, and the inner one competes with the outer for the eye.

pairs.dont: Wrap the whole page body in a card.
pairs.do: Let the page be the page; use cards for the things on it.
pairs.why: A card that contains everything separates nothing. The lift is a comparison — it only reads against an unlifted surface.

pairs.dont: Repeat the section heading as the card title.
pairs.do: Title the card only when the content needs naming.
pairs.why: A card is allowed to be just content. A title that echoes the heading above it costs a line and adds nothing.

pairs.dont: Scatter actions through the card — one in the header, two in the body, one in the footer.
pairs.do: Put per-card actions in the header, and the ones that finish the job in the footer.
pairs.why: Two places is a pattern people can learn. Four is a search.

pairs.dont: Make the whole card a link and put buttons inside it.
pairs.do: Either the card is the target, or it holds targets — not both.
pairs.why: A click inside a clickable card is ambiguous to the person and genuinely ambiguous in the markup; nested interactive elements are also invalid for assistive technology.

pairs.dont: Use sm to fit more words into the same space.
pairs.do: Use sm where cards repeat — a list, a grid, a sidebar — and default where one card carries a page.
pairs.why: The size changes padding, not type. Shrinking the padding to win room makes the content feel crowded rather than compact.
